title: PSB Cv 10 Cassava (VC 5): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: PSB Cv 10 Cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: PSB Cv 10 cassava is a cassava variety for Mindanao. 8 to 10 months to harvest, 44.8 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: PSB Cv 10 is a registered cassava variety, also sold or known as VC 5 or VC 5 cassava. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1993. It takes 8 to 10 months from planting to harvest, with 44.8 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for VC 5 or VC 5 cassava, this is the same cassava. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [cassava variety finder](/crop-varieties/cassava), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** 8 to 10 months from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 44.8 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about PSB Cv 10 cassava
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

PSB Cv 10 cassava takes 8 to 10 months from planting to harvest. That is 1.5 months faster than the average of the 42 cassava varieties with a day count, 10.5 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 44.8 t/ha beats the average of its group, 33.84. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up
Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit cassava fields most often: [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have yellow flesh and white skin. Dry matter is 33.6 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 20.3 percent.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** High HCN (bitter), starch millers prefer high cyanide types.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the starch mills' variety: over 3,000 ha in Lanao in the 1990s, planted for its high yield. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant PSB Cv 10 cassava

It is recommended for Mindanao. Pick by buyer first. Starch and feed plants pay for yield and starch content, while the table wants a sweet, low cyanide variety that boils soft. A high starch variety needs a buyer within a day of harvest, because the roots spoil fast.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is VC 5 the same as PSB Cv 10?
items.a: Yes. VC 5 is another name for PSB Cv 10. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 8 to 10 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 44.8 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for Mindanao. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of PSB Cv 10?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
